The South African DJ on Afro house's global rise, the townships that incubated it and why the sound should stay open to all. (Subscribe to our channel: https://www.youtube.com/residentadvisor ) Shimza grew up in Tembisa, a township east of Johannesburg, where as a kid he followed the DJs who played the area's stokvel parties. Members of these community savings clubs took turns hosting and competed to book the best DJs. Those DJs became local tastemakers, and some went on to play national radio and run the record shops that shaped grassroots South African house. He eventually broke out of that circuit to become one of Afro house's biggest exports. This year he brought his Shimza & Co residency back to Pacha for a second Ibiza season, and he now sells out shows for thousands from Amsterdam to Mexico City. Along the way he built Kunye, which started as a lockdown livestream and grew into a label and party platform for the next generation of African artists. In this Exchange with RA's content production lead Antonia Odunlami, Shimza weighs in on the growing debate over who Afro house belongs to and whether it needs to be reclaimed. His answer is clear: open it up. The pair unpack how South Africa turned global influences into sounds of its own, from kwaito to amapiano, and how streaming helped carry Afro house from township parties to the world's biggest stages. ----------------------- Website: https://ra.co Follow us: https://www.tiktok.com/@residentadvisor https://www.instagram.com/resident_advisor/ https://www.facebook.com/residentadvisor/ -----------------------

The Berghain resident on punk's ethos, choosing the difficult path and his new album, My Own Shadow. (Subscribe to our channel: https://www.youtube.com/residentadvisor ) Marcel Dettmann has become synonymous with Berghain and its primary cultural export: Berlin techno. He began DJing at Ostgut, Berghain's predecessor, in 1999. When Berghain opened its doors in 2004, he was one of its first residents, on a roster that grew to include luminaries like his longtime collaborator Ben Klock. In this RA Exchange, Dettmann talks about the long road from bedroom DJ to one of techno's leading figures: first falling in love with '80s new wave records, running a record store out of his mother's house, sharing vinyl with neighbourhood friends like future Berghain resident Marcel Fengler, and eventually landing behind the counter at Hard Wax, which he calls his "school". Dettmann has been a fixture on the techno circuit for more than 25 years, yet there are still sides of his artistry that fans may not know. My Own Shadow, an expanding project of EPs and visual work that now includes a full-length album, shows his creative world from another angle. He breaks down the album's cinematic imagery, reflects on the years it took to get where he is, and explains why the path that takes the most work is the one that pays off. My Own Shadow is out November 13th on !K7. ----------------------- Website: https://ra.co Follow us: https://www.tiktok.com/@residentadvisor https://www.instagram.com/resident_advisor/ https://www.facebook.com/residentadvisor/ -----------------------
